outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.question_text:
Write each statement using symbols.

(a) Line $JK$ is parallel to line $LM$.

(b) Line $UV$ is perpendicular to line $WX$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $JK \parallel LM$

The symbol $\parallel$ means parallel.

(b) $UV \perp WX$

The symbol $\perp$ means perpendicular.

Matching single arrowheads show $JK \parallel LM$.

Matching double arrowheads show $JL \parallel KM$.

The squares at $J$ and $K$ show $JL \perp JK$ and $KM \perp JK$.

Matching arrowheads show $JK \parallel LM \parallel NP$.

The three right-angle marks show $QR \perp JK$, $QR \perp LM$ and $QR \perp NP$.

Line $QR$ is perpendicular to all three.

examples.derivation: The source defines parallel notation and perpendicular notation at lines 1725–1728 and 1754–1756. Translating the given statements gives JK ∥ LM and UV ⟂ WX. No calculation, diagram or continuation gutter is required.

Independently reading the diagram: JK and LM have matching single arrowheads; JL and KM have matching double arrowheads. Thus JK ∥ LM and JL ∥ KM. The square at J lies between JL and JK, and the square at K lies between KM and JK, giving JL ⟂ JK and KM ⟂ JK. The coordinates agree with every marked relationship. This adapts the source example at lines 1779–1789 with different labels.

JK, LM and NP are horizontal lines with matching arrowheads, so JK ∥ LM ∥ NP. QR is vertical and has a right-angle square at each intersection, establishing QR ⟂ JK, QR ⟂ LM and QR ⟂ NP. ST is oblique and has no right-angle marks. This follows Guided Practice c at lines 1809–1814 and image203.png, using different labels and dimensions.
